text:
Recommendation: Don't shut down the note app to pivot fully. Instead, build AI agents into the existing product and validate the new direction before committing.
Why:
- You'd give up $16,000/month (~$192K/year) in recurring revenue from 40 paying teams.
- Churn is 2% monthly (~22% annually), which is healthy for SMB B2B SaaS — customers are staying.
- Those 40 teams are a distribution channel and feedback source that won't follow you to a new product after shutdown.
- "Investors love it" isn't a strategy; investors fund traction, not categories, and a 4-person team starting from zero in a crowded space is a weaker pitch than one with $192K ARR plus an AI expansion.
- "AI agent platform" isn't yet a defined product — no clear customer or differentiation from OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, Salesforce, and many funded startups.
- Your existing teams' knowledge in the product is exactly the context agents need — an advantage you'd be discarding.
Risks and unknowns:
- Shutting down is nearly impossible to reverse, unlike a pivot done while keeping the app running.
- Unclear whether the real driver is stalled growth, fundraising pressure, or the team losing interest in notes — this changes the analysis.
Next steps:
1. Build agent features into the note app (e.g., turning meeting notes into tasks/follow-ups/CRM updates, or answering questions across team knowledge) and charge for it as an add-on; gauge value within weeks.
2. Run the note app lean: one person on maintenance/support part-time, three people exploring the agent direction.
3. Validate before fully committing: run 15–20 interviews with target agent-product buyers and aim for 3–5 letters of intent or paid pilots.
4. Set an explicit kill criterion for the note app (e.g., wind it down if agent add-on revenue passes a set threshold, or if growth stalls for a set number of months) so any full pivot is deliberate, not reactive.
